Rule: if the first operand is truthy, JavaScript never evaluates the second operand.
Figure 46: Short-circuit evaluation. Both operators return an operand's actual value and stop as soon as the result is known.

9.3 Logical NOT (!) & Double NOT (!!)

Your Notes: Definition
  • Logical NOT is also called the negation operator.
  • It converts truthy values into false.
  • It converts falsy values into true.
  • It negates the value: true becomes false and false becomes true.
Truth Table
A!A
truefalse
falsetrue
Double NOT (!!): converts any value into its Boolean equivalent
console.log(!!10);        // → true
console.log(!!0);         // → false
console.log(!!"Hello");   // → true
console.log(!!"");        // → false
  • What happens: the first ! converts to boolean and flips it; the second flips it back.
  • Output: true, false, true, false.
  • ✅ Quick way to get a real boolean: !!value (same as Boolean(value)).

9.4 Logical Operators with Strings / Values

Your Notes: JavaScript returns the actual operand, NOT always true or false.
&& and || return operands
console.log("apple" && "banana");   // → "banana"  (both truthy → last)
console.log("" && "banana");        // → ""        (first falsy)
console.log("apple" || "banana");   // → "apple"   (first truthy)
console.log("" || "banana");        // → "banana"
console.log(10 && 20);              // → 20
console.log(10 || 20);              // → 10
console.log(0 && 20);               // → 0
console.log(0 || 20);               // → 20
console.log(null || "Default");     // → "Default"
console.log(undefined || "Guest");  // → "Guest"
// ✔ comment said "default" (lowercase); the output is "Default"
  • What happens: && and || return one of the OPERANDS, not true/false: && the first falsy (or the last), || the first truthy (or the last).
  • Output: banana, "", apple, banana, 20, 10, 0, 20, Default, Guest.
  • ✅ Default values: name || "Guest".
  • ⚠ || also replaces 0 and ""; use ?? if those are valid.
&& returns the first falsy value
console.log(null && "Hello");         // → null
console.log(10 && 20);                 // → 20
console.log(10 || 20);                 // → 10
console.log(false && "JavaScript");   // → false  (first falsy value)
  • What happens: && stops at the first falsy value.
  • Output: null, 20, 10, false.
|| returns the first truthy value (or the last value if all are falsy)
console.log(false || "JavaScript");    // → "JavaScript"

// "" (empty string) is falsy, and "Guest" is truthy (non-empty string)
console.log("" || "Guest");            // → "Guest"

// && returns the first falsy value, or the last value if all are truthy.
// "Hello" is truthy (non-empty string) and 100 is truthy (non-zero number),
// so since both are truthy, the operator returns the last operand: 100
console.log("Hello" && 100);           // → 100
  • What happens: || stops at the first truthy value; && returns the last if all are truthy.
  • Output: JavaScript, Guest, 100.
! and !!
// "JavaScript" is a non-empty string, so it is truthy.
// The first ! makes it false, and the second ! turns it back into true.
console.log(!!"JavaScript");   // → true

// Arrays are truthy, so ! (NOT) converts [] to false
console.log(![]);              // → false
  • What happens: !! gives the boolean value; ![] is false because an array is truthy.
  • Output: true, false.
JS मध्ये && आणि || नेहमी true/false देत नाहीत, तर operand ची खरी value परत देतात. && पहिली falsy value देतो (नसेल तर शेवटची), आणि || पहिली truthy value देतो (नसेल तर शेवटची). ! value उलटा करतो, आणि !! कोणत्याही value ला boolean मध्ये बदलतो.

10. Increment & Decrement Operators

Your Notes: Definition
  • The increment (++) operator increases the value of a variable by 1.
  • The decrement (--) operator decreases the value of a variable by 1.
  • These operators work only with variables (operands), not with constants or literals (5++ → SyntaxError; const c = 1; c++ → TypeError).
  • JS provides 2 types of increment (++) and decrement (--):
    1. Postfix increment and decrement operators (x++, x--)
    2. Prefix increment and decrement operators (++x, --x)
Operator TypeSyntaxDescription
Post-Incrementx++Return value first, then increment
Pre-Increment++xIncrement first, then return value
Post-Decrementx--Return value first, then decrement
Pre-Decrement--xDecrement first, then return value
  1. Increment: the operator adds one to its operand and returns the value before or after the increment, depending on where the operator is placed (post or pre).
  2. Decrement (--): the operator decrements (subtracts one from) its operand and returns the value before or after the decrement, depending on where the operator is placed.
FeaturePrefix (++x / --x)Postfix (x++ / x--)
Memory updatedFirstLater
Returned valueUpdated valueOriginal value
Execution orderUpdate → ReturnReturn → Update
Interview priorityVery HighVery High
Figure 47: Postfix returns the old value and then updates; prefix updates first and returns the new value.

10.1 Post-increment (x++)

Your Notes: The increment operator (++) adds 1 to its operand.
  • Post-increment (x++): the increment operator adds 1 to its operand after returning the value.
  • Definition: increments the variable after returning the current value.
  • Usage: the expression uses the original value, then the value is incremented.
  • Def: the post-increment operator means the expression is evaluated first using the original value of the variable, and then the variable's value is increased.
  • Returns the current value first, then increments the variable in memory.
Post-increment (your code, runs as-is with its own names)
let pNum = 10;
let pResult = pNum++;
console.log(pResult);   // → 10   uses the original value
console.log(pNum);      // → 11   incremented after

let pVal = 50;
let pRes = pVal++ + 5;
console.log(pRes);      // → 55   uses the original value (50 + 5)
console.log(pVal);      // → 51   incremented after
// ✔ Note: your original was commented out because num/result/val already existed; renamed here so it can run
  • What happens: x++ returns the OLD value, then adds 1.
  • Output: 10, 11, 55, 51.

10.2 Pre-increment (++x)

Your Notes:
  • Pre-increment (++x): the increment operator adds 1 to its operand before returning the value.
  • Increments the variable before returning the value.
  • Usage: the expression uses the incremented value.
  • The pre-increment operator means the variable's value is incremented first, and then the expression is evaluated using the new value.
  • Increments the value first, then returns the updated value.
Pre-increment
let n1 = 30;
let r1 = ++n1;
console.log(r1);        // → 31
console.log(n1);        // → 31

let val1 = 50;
let res11 = ++val1 + 5;
console.log(res11);     // → 56   (51 + 5)
console.log(val1);      // → 51
// ✔ was "++val + 5" (wrong variable) → printed 26, and val1 stayed 50
  • What happens: ++x adds 1 first, then returns the NEW value.
  • Output: 31, 31, 56, 51.
तुमच्या code मध्ये ++val1 ऐवजी ++val लिहिले होते, त्यामुळे वेगळा variable (val = 20) वाढला आणि उत्तर 26 आले. ++val1 केल्यावर बरोबर 56 आणि 51 येते.

10.3 Pre-decrement (--x)

Your Notes: The decrement operator (--) subtracts 1 from its operand and returns the value before or after the decrement. ✔ "subtracts 1 before returning the value" is true only for the prefix form; the intro applies to both forms."return करण्याआधी 1 वजा करतो" हे फक्त prefix (--x) साठी खरे आहे. postfix (x--) आधी value देतो आणि मग वजा करतो.
  • Pre-decrement (--x) definition: decrements the variable before returning the value.
  • Use: the expression uses the decremented value.
  • The pre-decrement operator means the variable's value is decremented first, and then the expression is evaluated using the new value.
  • Decrements the value first, then returns the updated value.
Pre-decrement
let x = 3;
let y = --x;
console.log(y);     // → 2   decremented first
console.log(x);     // → 2

let va = 50;
let re = --va + 5;
console.log(re);    // → 54  (49 + 5)
console.log(va);    // → 49
// ✔ was "--val + 5" (wrong variable) → printed 25, and va stayed 50
  • What happens: --x subtracts first, then returns.
  • Output: 2, 2, 54, 49.
इथेही --va ऐवजी --val लिहिले होते, त्यामुळे उत्तर 25 आले आणि va बदलला नाही. --va केल्यावर बरोबर 54 आणि 49 येते.

10.4 Post-decrement (x--)

Your Notes:
  • Post-decrement (x--): the decrement operator subtracts 1 from its operand after returning the value.
  • Definition: decrements the variable after returning the current value.
  • The expression uses the original value, then the variable is decremented.
  • The post-decrement expression is evaluated first using the original value of the variable, and then the variable's value is decremented.
  • Returns the current value first, then decrements the variable in memory.
Post-decrement
let x1 = 3;
let y1 = x1--;
console.log(y1);        // → 3   uses the original value
console.log(x1);        // → 2   decremented after

let val2 = 50;
let result2 = val2-- + 5;
console.log(result2);   // → 55  (50 + 5)
console.log(val2);      // → 49
  • What happens: x-- returns the old value, then subtracts.
  • Output: 3, 2, 55, 49.
Extra Details: classic tricky question 
let q = 5;
console.log(q++ + ++q);   // → 12   (5 + 7): q++ gives 5 (q→6), ++q makes q 7 and gives 7
console.log(q);           // → 7
  • What happens: left to right: q++ gives 5 (q becomes 6), then ++q makes 7 and gives 7.
  • Output: 12, 7.
  • ⚠ Mixing ++ in one expression is confusing; avoid in real code.
x++ (postfix): आधी जुनी value वापरतो, मग 1 वाढवतो. ++x (prefix): आधी 1 वाढवतो, मग नवीन value वापरतो. -- साठी सुद्धा हाच नियम आहे. लक्षात ठेवा: operator आधी (++x) = आधी बदल; operator नंतर (x++) = नंतर बदल.

11. Operator Precedence & Associativity

Extra Details: when one expression has many operators, precedence decides which runs first, and associativity decides the order among equal ones.
Priority (high → low)OperatorsAssociativity
1( ) groupingn/a
2. [] () ?. member / callleft → right
3x++ x--n/a
4! ~ + - ++x --x typeof void deleteright → left
5**right → left
6* / %left → right
7+ -left → right
8<< >> >>>left → right
9< <= > >= in instanceofleft → right
10== != === !==left → right
11& → ^ → |left → right
12&& → || / ??left → right
13? :right → left
14= += -= … &&= ||= ??=right → left
15, commaleft → right
2 + 3 * 4          // → 14   (* first)
(2 + 3) * 4        // → 20
2 ** 3 ** 2        // → 512  (right → left)
let a1, b1; a1 = b1 = 5;   // both 5 (= is right → left)
1 < 2 < 3          // → true   ((1<2)=true → 1 < 3)
3 > 2 > 1          // → false  ((3>2)=true → 1 > 1)
  • What happens: * before +; brackets first; ** and = work right-to-left; comparison chains go left-to-right, turning true into 1.
  • Output: 14, 20, 512, 5, true, false.
When in doubt, use parentheses. They make the code clearer.
एका expression मध्ये अनेक operators असतील तर precedence (प्राधान्य) ठरवते कोणता आधी चालेल (* आधी, + नंतर). समान प्राधान्य असल्यास associativity दिशा ठरवते (** आणि = उजवीकडून). शंका असल्यास ( ) वापरा.

12. Interview Questions (Detailed)

Q1. What is the difference between an expression and a statement?
  • An expression produces a value (2 + 3, x, a ? b : c). A statement performs an action (if, for, let x = 5;). Expressions can be used wherever a value is expected; statements cannot.
Q2. What is the difference between x++ and ++x?
  • Both add 1 to x. x++ returns the old value and then increments; ++x increments first and returns the new value. The difference only matters when the result is used inside a larger expression.
Q3. Why does ~5 equal -6?
  • ~ flips all 32 bits (1's complement). JS reads the result as a two's-complement signed integer, so ~x = -(x + 1), giving ~5 = -6.
Q4. What is the difference between >> and >>>?
  • >> copies the sign bit into the left, so negatives stay negative (-5 >> 1 = -3). >>> always fills the left with 0 and treats the value as unsigned, so -5 >>> 1 = 2147483645.
Q5. What is short-circuit evaluation?
  • && stops at the first falsy operand, and || stops at the first truthy operand. The remaining operands are not evaluated. This is used for defaults (x || "default") and guards (user && user.name).
Q6. Output-based questions
console.log(1 + "2" + 3);          // → "123"
console.log(1 + 2 + "3");          // → "33"
console.log("5" * "2");            // → 10
console.log(10 % 3, -10 % 3);      // → 1 -1
console.log(2 ** 3 ** 2);          // → 512
console.log(5 & 1, 4 & 1);         // → 1 0   (odd / even)
console.log(~~-3.9);               // → -3
console.log(-5 >> 1, -5 >>> 1);   // → -3 2147483645
console.log("b" > "a", "B" > "a"); // → true false
console.log(null || 0 || "" || "x"); // → "x"
console.log(1 && "a" && 0 && "b");  // → 0
let i = 1; console.log(i++ + i++); // → 3  (1 + 2), i is now 3
  • What happens: twelve mixed output questions on coercion, %, **, bits, string comparison, ||/&& and ++.
  • Output: "123", "33", 10, 1 -1, 512, 1 0, -3, -3 2147483645, true false, "x", 0, 3.
  • ✅ Revise before interviews.

1. Conditional Operator

Your Notes: Definition
  • The conditional operator (? :) is also called the ternary operator.
  • It is a shorthand way of writing an if...else statement (a concise way to write a simple if-else statement in programming).
  • It evaluates a condition and returns one value if the condition is true, and another value if the condition is false.
  • It is called the ternary operator because it works with three operands:
    1. condition
    2. value if true
    3. value if false
Definition: The conditional (ternary) operator is the only JavaScript operator that takes three operands: a condition, followed by ? and an expression to return if the condition is truthy, then : and an expression to return if it is falsy. It is an expression, so it always produces a value.
Ternary operator (? :) हा if...else चा छोटा (shorthand) प्रकार आहे. तो condition तपासतो: condition true असेल तर पहिली value आणि false असेल तर दुसरी value परत देतो. त्याला तीन भाग (operands) लागतात, म्हणून त्याला "ternary" (तीन) म्हणतात.

2. Syntax & the Three Operands

Your Notes: Syntax
  • condition ? expressionIfTrue : expressionIfFalse (the conditional (ternary) operator takes three operands). ✔ "three arguments" → "three operands". Arguments are values passed to a function; operators take operands.function ला दिलेल्या values ना arguments म्हणतात. operator सोबत वापरलेल्या values ना operands म्हणतात. म्हणून "three operands" हा बरोबर शब्द आहे.
  • Based on the condition, it returns an expression: variableName = (condition) ? value1 : value2
Figure 48: The three operands of the ternary operator.

3. How It Works

Your Notes: 
  Condition
      │
      ▼
Is condition true?
     / \
   Yes  No
    │    │
    ▼    ▼
 True   False
 Value  Value
  • What happens: [TODO: Explanation required]
  • Output: [TODO: Output required]
Figure 49: Ternary flow. Only ONE branch is evaluated; the other is skipped entirely.
Extra Details:
  • The condition doesn't need to be a boolean. It is truthy/falsy coerced (Chapter 3), so "" ? "a" : "b" → "b".
  • Only the chosen branch runs (short-circuit). true ? log("A") : log("B") prints only "A".
आधी condition तपासली जाते (ती truthy आहे की falsy). truthy असेल तर ? नंतरची value मिळते, falsy असेल तर : नंतरची value मिळते. दोन्हीपैकी फक्त एकच भाग चालतो.

4. Example 1: Ternary vs if…else

Your Notes (your code):
Ex. 1: Ternary operator
let age = 20;
let result = age >= 18 ? 'eligible for vote' : 'not eligible';

console.log(result);            // → "eligible for vote"
  • What happens: condition ? valueIfTrue : valueIfFalse; 20 >= 18 is true.
  • Output: eligible for vote.
  • ✅ One-line choice between two values.
Equivalent with if…else
let myAge = 17;

if (myAge >= 18) {
  console.log('eligible for vote');
} else {
  console.log('Not Eligible...');   // → "Not Eligible..."  (17 < 18)
}
  • What happens: the same choice written as if…else.
  • Output: Not Eligible...
Extra Details: the same logic, written both ways with the same variable: 
// if…else → a STATEMENT (needs a variable declared first)
let msg;
if (age >= 18) {
  msg = "eligible for vote";
} else {
  msg = "not eligible";
}

// ternary → an EXPRESSION (one line, can be used directly as a value)
const msg2 = age >= 18 ? "eligible for vote" : "not eligible";
console.log(`You are ${age >= 18 ? "adult" : "minor"}`);   // → "You are adult"
  • What happens: if…else is a statement (needs a variable first); a ternary is an expression, so it can sit inside const or a template literal.
  • Output: You are adult.
  • ✅ Ternary inside ${} for small UI texts.
Ternary एका line मध्ये value देतो, म्हणून तो थेट variable मध्ये, template literal मध्ये किंवा return मध्ये वापरता येतो. if...else हा statement आहे, तो value देत नाही. त्यामुळे त्याच्यासाठी आधी variable बनवावा लागतो.

5. Example 2: Nested Ternary Operator

Your Notes (your code):
Ex. 2: Nested ternary (grades)
let mark = 50;

let grade = mark >= 85 ? 'GRADE A' :
            mark >= 60 ? 'GRADE B' :
            mark >= 35 ? 'GRADE C' : 'FAIL';
// ✔ last value was "FALSE"; a grade result should be "FAIL"

console.log(grade);             // → "GRADE C"   (50 >= 35)
  • What happens: ternaries can be chained: the first true condition wins (85? 60? 35?).
  • Output: GRADE C.
  • ⚠ Long chains are hard to read; use if/else-if or a lookup table.
शेवटची value "FALSE" होती, जी boolean false सारखी वाटते आणि गोंधळ करते. marks 35 पेक्षा कमी असतील तर निकाल "FAIL" असायला हवा, म्हणून बदलले.
Figure 50: A nested ternary is a ladder, checked top to bottom; the first true condition wins.
Nested ternary म्हणजे एका ternary च्या false भागात दुसरा ternary. वरून खाली एक-एक condition तपासली जाते आणि पहिली true condition जिंकते. mark = 50: 85? नाही, 60? नाही, 35? हो, म्हणून "GRADE C".

6. Chaining Multiple Ternary Operators

Your Notes: you can also chain multiple ternary operators:
Nested inside the TRUE branch
const isMember  = true;
const isStudent = false;

const price = isMember ? (isStudent ? "5 USD" : "10 USD") : "15 USD";

console.log(price);             // → "10 USD"   (member, not a student)
  • What happens: a ternary inside the true branch of another.
  • Output: 10 USD.
  • ⚠ Nested ternaries need brackets and formatting to stay readable.
Extra Details: all combinations
isMemberisStudentprice
truetrue"5 USD"
truefalse"10 USD"
falseany"15 USD"
The parentheses are optional but make the nesting clear. Nesting inside the true branch is harder to read than a top-to-bottom chain, so keep the parentheses.
isMember true असेल तर आतला ternary (isStudent) तपासला जातो. false असेल तर थेट "15 USD" मिळते. isMember = true आणि isStudent = false, म्हणून उत्तर "10 USD".

7. Multiple Conditions

Your Notes: multiple conditions for displaying a message
Status message
const status = "offline";

const message =
  status === "online"  ? "You are online"  :
  status === "away"    ? "You are away"    :
  status === "offline" ? "You are offline" :
                         "Unknown status";

console.log(message);           // → "You are offline"
  • What happens: chained comparisons pick a message for the status.
  • Output: You are offline.
Example: greeting by time
const time = 13;

const greeting =
  time < 12 ? "Good Morning"   :
  time < 18 ? "Good Afternoon" :
              "Good Evening";

console.log(greeting);          // → "Good Afternoon"   (13 < 18)
  • What happens: 13 isn't < 12, but is < 18.
  • Output: Good Afternoon.
Extra Details: a cleaner alternative for many fixed values (object lookup) 
const messages = {
  online:  "You are online",
  away:    "You are away",
  offline: "You are offline",
};

const message2 = messages[status] ?? "Unknown status";
console.log(message2);          // → "You are offline"
  • What happens: a lookup object replaces the ternary chain; ?? gives the fallback.
  • Output: You are offline.
  • ✅ Cleaner and easy to extend with new statuses.
When one variable is compared with many fixed values, an object lookup (or switch) is easier to read and extend than a long ternary chain.
अनेक conditions असल्यास ternary एका खाली एक (ladder) लिहा, म्हणजे वाचायला सोपे जाते. पण एकाच variable च्या अनेक fixed values असतील तर object lookup किंवा switch जास्त चांगले.

8. Expression vs Statement & Best Practices

FeatureTernary (? :)if…else
TypeExpression: produces a valueStatement: performs an action
Returns a value?✅ Yes❌ No
Use inside const x = …, return, template literals, JSX✅ Yes❌ No
Multiple statements per branch❌ Not practical✅ Yes
Best forSimple choice between two valuesComplex logic, many lines, side effects
Readability with many conditions⚠ Gets hard when deeply nested✅ Clear
Extra Details: best practices
  • Use a ternary to choose a value, not to run side effects: prefer const x = c ? a : b over c ? doA() : doB().
  • Avoid nesting more than 2 levels. Use if…else, switch or an object lookup instead.
  • Format chains as a vertical "ladder", one condition per line.
  • For defaults, ?? is often simpler: name ?? "Guest" instead of name !== null && name !== undefined ? name : "Guest".
  • Ternary is right-associative: a ? b : c ? d : e means a ? b : (c ? d : e).
Ternary हा expression आहे (value देतो), तर if...else हा statement आहे (काम करतो). दोन values मधून एक निवडायची असेल तर ternary वापरा. खूप मोठे logic किंवा अनेक lines असतील तर if...else वापरा. 2 पेक्षा जास्त levels चे nesting टाळा.

9. Interview Questions (Detailed)

Q1. What is the ternary operator, and why is it called "ternary"?
  • It is the conditional operator condition ? a : b. It is called ternary because it is the only JS operator that takes three operands: the condition, the value if truthy and the value if falsy.
Q2. What is the difference between the ternary operator and if…else?
  • The ternary is an expression that evaluates to a value, so it can be assigned, returned or embedded in a template literal. if…else is a statement that controls which block runs and does not produce a value. Use the ternary for simple value choices and if…else for complex logic.
Q3. Can the ternary operator be used without an else part?
  • No, both ? and : are required. For "only if true" logic, use if or condition && doSomething().
Q4. Is the condition converted to a boolean?
  • Yes, it uses truthy/falsy rules. 0 ? "yes" : "no" → "no", and [] ? "yes" : "no" → "yes".
Q5. Output-based questions
console.log(5 > 3 ? "A" : "B");               // → "A"
console.log("" ? "truthy" : "falsy");          // → "falsy"
console.log(null ?? 0 ? "yes" : "no");         // → "no"    (null ?? 0 → 0 → falsy)
const n = 0;
console.log(n ? n : "default");                // → "default" (0 is falsy!)
console.log(n ?? "default");                   // → 0         (?? keeps 0)
let x = 10;
let y = x > 5 ? x > 8 ? "big" : "medium" : "small";
console.log(y);                                // → "big"
console.log(typeof (true ? 1 : "1"));          // → "number"
  • What happens: seven ternary output questions: precedence (?? before ?:), 0 is falsy, nested ternary, the result type.
  • Output: A, falsy, no, default, 0, big, number.

10. Quick Revision Summary

ConceptOne-line Summary
Ternarycondition ? ifTrue : ifFalse: shorthand for a simple if…else
Why "ternary"The only operator with 3 operands
ConditionCoerced to truthy/falsy
EvaluationOnly the chosen branch runs
Nested / chainedA ladder checked top to bottom; the first true condition wins
Expression vs statementTernary returns a value; if…else does not
Best practiceUse it to choose values; max ~2 levels; otherwise if/switch/object lookup
थोडक्यात: condition ? true-value : false-value. Ternary एका line मध्ये value निवडतो. nested ternary ladder सारखा वरून खाली तपासला जातो. खूप nesting झाले तर if...else, switch किंवा object lookup वापरा.

1. Nullish Coalescing Operator (??)

Your Notes: Definition
  • The nullish coalescing (??) operator returns the right-hand value only when the left-hand value is null or undefined.
  • If the left-hand value is anything else, even 0, false or "", it returns the left-hand value.
  • Syntax: leftValue ?? rightValue;
Definition: The nullish coalescing operator (??, ES2020) is a logical operator that returns its right-hand operand when its left-hand operand is nullish (null or undefined), and otherwise returns its left-hand operand. It is used to provide default values without replacing valid falsy values like 0, "" or false.
?? operator फक्त डावी value null किंवा undefined असेल तेव्हाच उजवी (default) value देतो. डावी value 0, false, "" असली तरी ती "valid" मानली जाते आणि तीच परत मिळते. "Nullish" म्हणजे null किंवा undefined.

2. Q. How Does It Work?

Your Notes: 
      Left Value
          │
          ▼
Is it null or undefined?
         / \
       Yes  No
        │    │
        ▼    ▼
   Return   Return
   Right    Left
   Value    Value
  • What happens: [TODO: Explanation required]
  • Output: [TODO: Output required]
Figure 51: How ?? works. Only null and undefined trigger the default value.

3. Examples

Your Notes (your code):
Ex. 1: left value is null → right value
let name = null;

// If the left-hand value is null or undefined, it returns the right-hand value.
// Here the left-hand value is null, so it returns "Guest" (the right-hand value).
console.log(name ?? "Guest");        // → "Guest"
  • What happens: ?? returns the right side only when the left side is null or undefined.
  • Output: Guest.
Ex. 2: left value is a real value → left value
let userName = 'vishal';

// If the left-hand value is a string, 0, false or '', it returns the left-hand value.
console.log(userName ?? 'Guest');    // → "vishal"
  • What happens: left side has a value, so it is kept.
  • Output: vishal.
name null आहे, म्हणून ?? उजवी value "Guest" देतो. userName मध्ये 'vishal' आहे (null/undefined नाही), म्हणून तीच value मिळते.

4. Q. Why Not Use || ?

Your Notes:
Suppose count = 0 is a VALID value
let count = 0;

console.log(count || 100);   // → 100   ❌ 0 is falsy, so || replaces it
// It returns 100, but 0 may be a valid value, so use ?? (nullish coalescing operator).

console.log(count ?? 100);   // → 0     ✅ 0 is not null/undefined, so it is kept
// Output is 0: zero is not null and not undefined, so ?? returns zero.
  • What happens: || treats 0 as missing and replaces it; ?? keeps 0 because it isn't null/undefined.
  • Output: 100, 0.
  • ✅ Use ?? when 0, "" or false are valid values.
Figure 52: || treats every falsy value as missing; ?? treats only null and undefined as missing.
|| प्रत्येक falsy value (0, "", false) ला "value नाही" समजतो, म्हणून count = 0 असताना 100 देतो. पण 0 ही खरी value असू शकते (उदा. 0 items, 0 marks). ?? फक्त null/undefined लाच "value नाही" समजतो, म्हणून 0 तसाच ठेवतो.
Extra Details: real-world cases where || is a bug 
const settings = { volume: 0, title: "", darkMode: false };

settings.volume   || 50      // → 50     ❌ user chose mute (0)
settings.volume   ?? 50      // → 0      ✅
settings.title    || "Home"  // → "Home" (is "" allowed? then use ??)
settings.darkMode ?? true    // → false  ✅ user turned it off
  • What happens: settings where 0, "" and false are real choices: || breaks them, ?? keeps them.
  • Output: 50, 0, Home, false.

5. Another Examples

Your Notes: 
console.log(false ?? true);                // → false   (false is not nullish)
console.log(undefined ?? 'vishal');        // → "vishal"
console.log(null ?? 'Yes have Value');     // → "Yes have Value"
  • What happens: false is not nullish, so ?? keeps it; undefined and null are replaced.
  • Output: false, vishal, Yes have Value.
Extra Details: more cases
Expression??||
0 ?? 5 / 0 || 505
"" ?? "d" / "" || "d""""d"
false ?? true / false || truefalsetrue
NaN ?? 5 / NaN || 5NaN5
null ?? 5 / null || 555
undefined ?? 5 / undefined || 555
The two operators differ only for 0, "", false and NaN (and -0, 0n).

6. Differences between ?? vs || vs &&

Your Notes:
  • || treats all falsy values (0, false, "", null, undefined, NaN) as missing.
  • ?? treats only null and undefined as missing. (Missing, i.e. null or undefined? → use the default value.)
  • && returns the first falsy value or, if all values are truthy, the last value. It is commonly used for conditional execution. (Truthy? → continue; falsy? → stop immediately.)
Feature?? (Nullish Coalescing)|| (Logical OR)&& (Logical AND)
DefinitionReturns the right value only when the left value is null or undefined.Returns the left value if it is truthy; otherwise returns the right value.Returns the first falsy value. If all values are truthy, returns the last value.
PurposeProvide a default value only when the value is missing.Provide a fallback value for any falsy value.Execute or return the next expression only if the previous one is truthy.
Checks fornull, undefinedAll falsy values (false, 0, "", NaN, null, undefined)All falsy values (false, 0, "", NaN, null, undefined)
ReturnsLeft value if not null/undefined; otherwise right.Left value if truthy; otherwise right value.First falsy value OR last truthy value.
Short-circuitYesYesYes
Best use caseDefault valuesFallback valuesConditional execution
Introduced inES2020ES1ES1
Figure 53: The question each operator asks about its left value.
?? विचारतो "value null/undefined आहे का?" (हो असेल तर default). || विचारतो "value truthy आहे का?" (नाही तर fallback). && विचारतो "truthy आहे का?" (हो असेल तरच पुढे जा, नाहीतर तिथेच थांबून ती falsy value दे). तिघेही short-circuit करतात, म्हणजे गरज नसेल तर उजवी बाजू चालवत नाहीत.
Extra Details: && for conditional execution 
const user = { isAdmin: true, name: "Vishal" };

user.isAdmin && console.log("Show admin panel");   // runs only if truthy
const nameLen = user && user.name && user.name.length;   // → 6
// modern version of the same guard:
const nameLen2 = user?.name?.length;                        // → 6
  • What happens: && as a guard: the right side runs only when the left is truthy; ?. does the same more cleanly.
  • Output: Show admin panel, 6, 6.

7. Logical Assignment: ??=, ||=, &&=

Extra Details (ES2021): each of these operators has an assignment form that assigns only when needed.
Logical assignment operators
let a;          a ??= 5;     // → 5   (a was undefined → assign)
let b = 0;      b ??= 5;     // → 0   (0 is not nullish → keep)
let c = 0;      c ||= 7;     // → 7   (0 is falsy → assign)
let d = "hi";   d &&= "bye"; // → "bye" (d was truthy → assign)

// Same as:
// a ??= 5   ⟺   a ?? (a = 5)
// c ||= 7   ⟺   c || (c = 7)
// d &&= "x" ⟺   d && (d = "x")
  • What happens: ??= assigns only if the variable is null/undefined; ||= if falsy; &&= if truthy.
  • Output: 5, 0, 7, "bye".
  • ✅ Short default-setting: options.timeout ??= 3000.
a ??= 5 म्हणजे "a null/undefined असेल तरच 5 दे". ||= falsy असल्यावर value देतो, आणि &&= truthy असल्यावर value देतो.

8. Mixing ?? with || / &&

Extra Details: JavaScript does not allow ?? to be mixed directly with || or &&, because the intended order would be unclear. Use parentheses:
Example 1
// null || undefined ?? "x";        // ❌ SyntaxError: Unexpected token '??'
(null || undefined) ?? "x";         // → "x"   ✅
null || (undefined ?? "x");         // → "x"   ✅
  • What happens: mixing ?? with || or && without brackets is a SyntaxError; brackets make the order clear.
  • Output: x, x.
?? together with ?. is very common:
// ?? together with ?. is very common:
const user = {};
user.profile?.name ?? "No name";    // → "No name"
  • What happens: ?. returns undefined for the missing profile, then ?? supplies a default.
  • Output: No name.
  • ✅ The standard safe-read pattern.
(verified in Node)
?? ला || किंवा && सोबत brackets शिवाय वापरल्यास SyntaxError येतो. ( ) लावून कोणता भाग आधी चालवायचा ते स्पष्ट करा. ?. आणि ?? अनेकदा एकत्र वापरले जातात.

9. Interview: ?: vs ?. vs ??

Your Notes:
OperatorNameDefinitionExample
?:Conditional (Ternary) OperatorA shorthand for if...else. It evaluates a condition and returns one of two values based on whether the condition is true or false.age >= 18 ? "Adult" : "Minor"
?.Optional ChainingSafely accesses object properties or methods. If any part of the chain is null or undefined, it returns undefined instead of throwing an error.user?.address?.city
??Nullish CoalescingReturns the right-hand value only if the left-hand value is null or undefined; otherwise it returns the left-hand value.name ?? "Guest"
?: → एका ओळीत if...else लिहिण्यासाठी.
?. → Object ची property सुरक्षितपणे (safe) access करण्यासाठी. Error येत नाही.
?? → फक्त null किंवा undefined असल्यास default value देण्यासाठी.
  • ?? → "Is it null or undefined?" If yes, use the default value.
  • || → "Is it truthy?" If not, use the fallback value.
  • && → "Continue only if it's truthy." If it's falsy, stop immediately and return that value.
Extra Details: optional chaining forms 
const user = { address: null, greet() { return "hi"; } };

user?.address?.city      // → undefined  (no TypeError)
user.address.city        // ❌ TypeError: Cannot read properties of null
user.greet?.()           // → "hi"       (call only if the method exists)
user.missing?.()         // → undefined
const arr = null;
arr?.[0]                 // → undefined  (safe index access)
  • What happens: ?. stops (returning undefined) when the left side is null/undefined: for properties, method calls ?.() and indexes ?.[].
  • Output: undefined, TypeError (without ?.), hi, undefined, undefined.

10. Interview Questions (Detailed)

Q1. What is the nullish coalescing operator? How is it different from ||?
  • a ?? b returns b only when a is null or undefined. a || b returns b when a is any falsy value (0, "", false, NaN, null, undefined). Use ?? when 0, "" or false are valid values, such as counts, prices, empty input or boolean settings.
Q2. What does "nullish" mean?
  • A nullish value is either null or undefined, and nothing else. Every nullish value is falsy, but not every falsy value is nullish.
Q3. Does ?? short-circuit?
  • Yes. If the left side is not nullish, the right side is never evaluated: "x" ?? expensive() doesn't call expensive().
Q4. Why does a || b ?? c throw a SyntaxError?
  • The specification forbids mixing ?? with || or && without parentheses, to avoid confusion about precedence. Write (a || b) ?? c or a || (b ?? c).
Q5. Output-based questions
console.log(0 ?? "default");            // → 0
console.log(0 || "default");            // → "default"
console.log("" ?? "empty");             // → ""
console.log(null ?? undefined ?? "x");  // → "x"
console.log(false || null || "last");   // → "last"
console.log(1 && 2 && 3);             // → 3
console.log(1 && 0 && 3);             // → 0
console.log(null?.x ?? "safe");         // → "safe"
let v = 0; v ||= 10; console.log(v);    // → 10
let w = 0; w ??= 10; console.log(w);    // → 0
  • What happens: ten output questions comparing ?? with || and &&, plus ||= vs ??=.
  • Output: 0, default, "", x, last, 3, 0, safe, 10, 0.

Why ?? over ||Keeps valid 0, "" and false

Mixing rule?? with || / && needs parentheses

1. Optional Chaining (?.)

Your Notes: Definition
  • The optional chaining operator (?.) allows you to safely access the properties or methods of an object without throwing an error when the value before ?. is null or undefined. ✔ "if a property is null or undefined" → it checks the value on the LEFT of ?. (the object you are reading from), not the property you are reading.?. हा डावीकडील value (object) null/undefined आहे का ते तपासतो, वाचत असलेली property नाही. उदा. user?.name मध्ये user तपासला जातो.
  • If any part of the chain is null or undefined, JavaScript immediately returns undefined instead of throwing a TypeError.
Definition: Optional chaining (?., ES2020) accesses a property, index or method call only if the value before it is not nullish. If that value is null or undefined, the whole expression short-circuits and returns undefined instead of throwing a TypeError.
Optional Chaining (?.) म्हणजे safe property access. जर object किंवा property उपलब्ध नसेल, तर JavaScript error देत नाही, तर undefined परत करते. ?. च्या डावीकडची value null/undefined असेल तर पुढची साखळी (chain) तिथेच थांबते.

Your Notes: 
          user
            ↓
Is user null or undefined?
            │
        Yes │
            ▼
    Return undefined
       (No Error)
  • What happens: [TODO: Explanation required]
  • Output: [TODO: Output required]
Figure 54: How ?. works. It checks the value on its left and stops safely if that value is nullish.

3. Q. Why Do We Need Optional Chaining?

Your Notes:
Without ?. vs with ?.
// Suppose
let user = null;

// console.log(user.name);
// ❌ TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'name'), because user = null,
//    so there is no property called name.

// Using optional chaining, it returns undefined instead of a TypeError.
console.log(user?.name);       // → undefined   (no error occurs)
  • What happens: reading a property of null throws, but ?. returns undefined instead.
  • Output: undefined.
Figure 55: Normal access vs optional chaining on a null object.
user = null असताना user.name लिहिल्यास TypeError येतो आणि program थांबतो. user?.name लिहिल्यास JS शांतपणे undefined देतो आणि program पुढे चालू राहतो. API data, form data किंवा optional settings मध्ये value नसू शकते, म्हणून ?. उपयोगी आहे.
Extra Details: the old way vs ?. 
// Before ES2020 (&& guard chain)
const city1 = user && user.address && user.address.city;

// With optional chaining
const city2 = user?.address?.city;      // same result, much shorter
  • What happens: the old && chain and ?. give the same result; ?. is shorter.
  • Output: (no output).

4. Example 1: Nested Objects

Your Notes (your code):
Ex. 1: nested object
let userData = {
  name: 'vishal',
  address: {
    city: 'pune',
    zipCode: 412401,
  }
};

console.log(userData.age);                    // → undefined  (missing property; no ?. needed)
console.log(userData?.address?.street);       // → undefined  (street doesn't exist)
console.log(userData?.address?.zipCode);      // → 412401
console.log(userData?.address?.locality);     // → undefined
  • What happens: missing properties give undefined; ?. protects each step of the path.
  • Output: undefined, undefined, 412401, undefined.
  • ⚠ ?. isn't needed when the object surely exists (userData.age).
Extra Details: when is ?. really needed?
  • Reading a missing property from an object that exists already gives undefined without an error (userData.age).
  • The error happens only when you go one level deeper into something that is undefined or null:
// userData.contact.phone;     // ❌ TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'phone')
userData.contact?.phone;        // → undefined ✅  (put ?. after the part that may be missing)
  • What happens: contact is missing, so .phone on undefined throws; put ?. right after the part that may be missing.
  • Output: undefined.
Rule: put ?. right after the value that might be null or undefined.
अस्तित्वात असलेल्या object ची नसलेली property वाचल्यास (userData.age) error येत नाही, फक्त undefined मिळते. error तेव्हाच येतो जेव्हा undefined च्या आत जायचा प्रयत्न होतो (userData.contact.phone). म्हणून जी value नसू शकते, तिच्या नंतर ?. लावा.

Your Notes (your code):
?. with an array element
let users = [
  {
    name: 'vishal',
    age: 30
  }
];

console.log(users[1]?.name);    // → undefined   (users[1] doesn't exist; no error)
  • What happens: users[1] doesn't exist; ?. stops before reading .name.
  • Output: undefined.
Extra Details: the ?.[ ] form, for when the array itself may be null or undefined: 
let list = null;
console.log(list?.[0]);             // → undefined   (safe index access)
console.log(list?.length ?? 0);     // → 0           (?. + ?? for a default)
// console.log(list[0]);            // ❌ TypeError
  • What happens: ?.[] guards index access; combined with ?? for a default.
  • Output: undefined, 0.
users[1]?.name protects the element; users?.[1] protects the array. Use users?.[1]?.name to protect both.
users[1] अस्तित्वात नाही, म्हणून users[1]?.name ला undefined मिळते. array स्वतःच null असू शकत असेल तर arr?.[0] हा प्रकार वापरा.

6. Optional Chaining with Methods

Your Notes (your code):
?.() with a method
let person = {
  // method greet
  greet() {
    return 'Welcome to user';
  }
};

console.log(person.greet());    // → "Welcome to user"
console.log(person.add?.());    // → undefined   (add doesn't exist, so it is not called)
// console.log(person.add());   // ❌ TypeError: person.add is not a function
// ✔ return text was "Welcom to user"
  • What happens: ?.() calls the method only if it exists.
  • Output: Welcome to user, undefined.
  • ✅ Optional callbacks / plugin hooks.
return मधील "Welcom" ही spelling चूक होती, ती "Welcome" केली.
  • Optional Chaining (?.) म्हणजे safe property access.
  • जर object किंवा property उपलब्ध नसेल, तर JavaScript error देत नाही, तर undefined परत करते.
Extra Details: obj.method?.() calls the method only if it is not null/undefined. It still throws if the property exists but is not a function: 
const cfg = { onSave: null, name: "x" };
cfg.onSave?.();     // → undefined ✅  (optional callbacks)
// cfg.name?.();    // ❌ TypeError: cfg.name is not a function (a string exists!)
  • What happens: ?.() checks only for null/undefined: a string is not a function, so calling it still throws.
  • Output: undefined.
  • ⚠ ?.() doesn't check the TYPE.

7. The 3 Forms & Short-Circuiting

FormSyntaxUseExample
Propertyobj?.propRead a property safelyuser?.name
Bracket / indexobj?.[expr]Dynamic key or array indexarr?.[0], obj?.["first-name"]
Callfn?.(args)Call only if it existsperson.add?.()
Figure 56: Short-circuiting. Once ?. meets null or undefined, the rest of the chain is skipped.
Extra Details: short-circuit proof 
let user2 = null;
console.log(user2?.name.first);   // → undefined (no error, even though .first has no ?.)

let calls = 0;
const f = () => { calls++; return 1; };
null?.[f()];
console.log(calls);               // → 0   (f() was never called)
  • What happens: once ?. finds null, the WHOLE rest of the chain is skipped (short-circuit), including later property reads and function calls.
  • Output: undefined, 0.
?. ला null/undefined मिळाले की पुढची संपूर्ण chain (उजवीकडील सगळे भाग) चालवलीच जात नाही. म्हणून user?.address.city मध्ये .city वर ?. नसतानाही error येत नाही.

8. Limits & Best Practices

Extra Details:
  • Cannot assign: user?.name = "x" → ❌ SyntaxError: Invalid left-hand side in assignment (verified in Node).
  • Only null/undefined count: 0?.toFixed(1), ""?.length and false?.toString() work normally, because they are not nullish.
  • Combine with ?? for defaults: user?.address?.city ?? "Unknown".
  • Don't overuse it: if a value must exist, using ?. hides the bug. Use it only for values that are genuinely optional (API responses, optional config, callbacks).
  • Works with delete: delete user?.name is allowed.
Real-world: API response
const response = { data: { user: { profile: null } } };

const avatar = response?.data?.user?.profile?.avatar ?? "default.png";
console.log(avatar);            // → "default.png"

const firstTag = response.data?.tags?.[0] ?? "no tags";
console.log(firstTag);          // → "no tags"
  • What happens: deep API data where any level may be missing: ?. at each step, ?? for the default.
  • Output: default.png, no tags.
  • ✅ Safe rendering of server data.
?. ने value वाचता येते, पण त्याला value देता (assign) येत नाही. फक्त null/undefined वरच ?. थांबतो; 0, "", false वर नाही. default value साठी ?. सोबत ?? वापरा. जी value नक्की असायलाच हवी तिथे ?. वापरू नका, नाहीतर bug लपतो.

9. Interview Questions (Detailed)

Q1. What is optional chaining, and what problem does it solve?
  • ?. (ES2020) safely reads nested properties, indexes or methods. If the value before it is null or undefined, it returns undefined instead of throwing "Cannot read properties of null/undefined". It replaces long a && a.b && a.b.c guard chains.
Q2. What are the three syntax forms?
  • obj?.prop, obj?.[expr] and func?.(args).
Q3. What is short-circuiting in optional chaining?
  • When ?. finds null/undefined, the entire rest of the chain, including function calls and index expressions, is skipped and the result is undefined.
Q4. Can you use optional chaining on the left side of an assignment?
  • No, obj?.a = 1 is a SyntaxError. Check first: if (obj) obj.a = 1;.
Q5. Difference between ?. and ??
  • ?. safely reads from something that may be nullish and gives undefined. ?? replaces a nullish value with a default. They are often used together: user?.name ?? "Guest".
Q6. Output-based questions
const o = { a: { b: 0 }, list: [], fn: null };
console.log(o?.a?.b);            // → 0
console.log(o.x?.y.z);           // → undefined (short-circuit)
console.log(o.list?.[0]);        // → undefined
console.log(o.fn?.());           // → undefined
console.log(o.a?.b ?? 10);       // → 0   (0 is not nullish)
console.log(o.a?.b || 10);       // → 10
console.log(typeof o.missing?.x); // → "undefined"
// o.a?.b = 5;                   // ❌ SyntaxError
  • What happens: eight output questions: 0 survives ?? but not ||, short-circuit, ?. can't be used on the left of =.
  • Output: 0, undefined, undefined, undefined, 0, 10, "undefined".

10. Quick Revision Summary

ConceptOne-line Summary
?.Safe access: undefined instead of a TypeError when the left side is null/undefined (ES2020)
Formsa?.b, a?.[i], a.f?.()
Short-circuitOnce nullish is found, the rest of the chain is skipped
Missing propertyAlready undefined; ?. matters when you go one level deeper
Only nullish0, "", false still continue normally
AssignmentNot allowed (SyntaxError)
With ??a?.b ?? "default"
थोडक्यात: ?. म्हणजे "असेल तरच पुढे जा, नसेल तर undefined दे". तीन प्रकार आहेत: a?.b, a?.[i], a.f?.(). default value साठी ?? सोबत वापरा. value देण्यासाठी (assignment) ?. वापरता येत नाही.
Chapter 19: Spread Operator (...)Copy · merge · function arguments · strings · key conflicts · rest vs spread
CHAPTER 19 INDEX
  1. What is the Spread Operator?
  2. Use Cases with Arrays
  3. Spread with Function Calls
  4. Copying & Merging Objects
  5. Key Conflicts: the Last One Wins
  6. Spread with Strings
  7. Rest vs Spread
  8. Interview Questions & Revision

1. Spread Operator

Your Notes (14_spreadOperator.js/spread.js):
  1. The spread operator (...) in JavaScript is used to unpack or expand elements from arrays, objects or iterables (i.e. it allows you to expand or spread elements).
  2. It's a powerful feature for copying, merging (i.e. combining data) and expanding data structures.
  3. Syntax: ...iterable (for example [...arr], {...obj}, fn(...args)) ✔ "syntax: ...spread". The thing after ... is the array/object/iterable being spread.... नंतर जो array, object किंवा iterable येतो तोच spread होतो. "spread" हा शब्द syntax चा भाग नाही.
  4. The spread operator does not create a reference to the original array: the new array is a different array (arr !== newArr).
  5. This is because the new array is a separate instance with its own values, copied at the time of creation. ✔ true only at the TOP level. Spread makes a SHALLOW copy: nested arrays/objects inside are still the SAME references (verified in Node).spread फक्त shallow copy करतो. बाहेरचा array नवीन असतो, पण आतले nested arrays/objects अजूनही तेच (shared) असतात. पूर्ण copy साठी structuredClone() वापरा.
Definition: Spread syntax ... expands an iterable (array, string, Set, Map) into individual elements in array literals and function calls, and expands an object's own enumerable properties into an object literal. It always copies shallowly.
Figure 57: Spread unpacks an iterable into individual elements.
Spread operator (...) array, string किंवा object ला "उघडून" त्याचे घटक वेगवेगळे करतो. copy करणे, merge करणे आणि function ला arguments देणे यासाठी वापरतात. पण copy shallow असते, म्हणजे आतले objects shared राहतात.

2. Use Cases with Arrays

Your Notes:
1. copying an array: used to create a copy of an array
// # 1. copying an array: used to create a copy of an array
let arr = [1, 2, 3, 4];
let newArr = [...arr];
console.log("copied arr", newArr);   // → copied arr [1, 2, 3, 4]
  • What happens: [...arr] creates a new array with the same items.
  • Output: [1, 2, 3, 4].
  • ✅ Copy before sort/reverse so the original stays unchanged.
  • ⚠ Shallow: nested arrays/objects are still shared.
2. merging arrays: used to combine multiple arrays into a new array (merging arrays)
// # 2. merging arrays: used to combine multiple arrays into a new array (merging arrays)
let array = [...arr, ...newArr];
console.log(array);                  // → [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4]
// ✔ "merging marry" → merging arrays
  • What happens: spreading two arrays inside [] joins them.
  • Output: [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4].
  • ✅ Clearer than concat; items can be inserted anywhere: [0, ...a, 5].

3. Spread with Function Calls

Your Notes: in a function call, the spread operator is used to spread the elements of an array (or any iterable) as individual arguments to the function. 
let number = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7];
console.log([...number]);                  // → [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7]   (a new array)
console.log(...number);                    // → 1 2 3 4 5 6 7           (7 separate arguments)
console.log("max no :", Math.max(...number));   // → max no : 7
// Math.max(number) → NaN, because the whole array would be ONE argument
  • What happens: inside [] spread makes a new array; inside a call it turns the items into separate arguments, so Math.max gets 7 numbers.
  • Output: [1…7], 1 2 3 4 5 6 7, max no : 7.
  • ⚠ Spreading a huge array into a call can exceed the argument limit; use reduce for very large arrays.

4. Copying & Merging Objects

Your Notes:
copying an object
// # copying an object
let user = {
  name: "vishal",
  age: 25,
  education: "BE",
};
let newUser = { ...user };
console.log(newUser);   // → { name: 'vishal', age: 25, education: 'BE' }
  • What happens: { ...user } copies all own properties into a new object.
  • Output: { name: 'vishal', age: 25, education: 'BE' }.
merging objects
// # merging objects
const person = { name: "Vishal" };
const info = { age: 25 };
const merged = { ...person, ...info };
console.log(merged);    // → { name: 'Vishal', age: 25 }
  • What happens: spreading two objects merges their properties.
  • Output: { name: 'Vishal', age: 25 }.

5. Key Conflicts: the Last One Wins

Your Notes: if there is a key conflict while merging, the last one wins.
  1. If you use the spread operator to combine two objects and both objects have the same property, the property from the first object is overridden by the property from the 2nd object.
const x = { a: 1, b: 2 };
const y = { b: 3 };
const result = { ...x, ...y };   // b: 3 overwrites b: 2
console.log(result);             // → { a: 1, b: 3 }
// use it for defaults: { ...defaults, ...userOptions }
  • What happens: when both have the same key, the later one wins.
  • Output: { a: 1, b: 3 }.
  • ✅ Defaults pattern: { ...defaults, ...userOptions }.
merge करताना दोन objects मध्ये तीच key असल्यास नंतर लिहिलेल्या (शेवटच्या) object ची value राहते.

6. Spread with a String

Your Notes: the spread operator can be used to split or unpack a string into individual characters in an array. 
let name = "vishal";
console.log(...name);     // → v i s h a l
console.log([...name]);   // → ['v', 'i', 's', 'h', 'a', 'l']
  • What happens: a string is iterable, so spread splits it into characters.
  • Output: v i s h a l, ['v','i','s','h','a','l'].
Extra Details (verified in Node) 
const nested = [[1], [2]];
const copy = [...nested];
copy[0].push(99);
console.log(nested[0]);              // → [1, 99]   (shallow copy: inner array shared)
console.log([...new Set([1, 1, 2])]);   // → [1, 2]   (remove duplicates)
console.log({ ..."hi" });            // → { '0': 'h', '1': 'i' }
console.log({ ...null, ...undefined }); // → {}   (ignored in object literals)
// [...{ a: 1 }] → TypeError: object is not iterable (plain objects can be spread only into { })
  • What happens: spread copies only one level (the inner array is shared); Set + spread removes duplicates; a string spreads into an object by index; null/undefined are ignored in {…}; plain objects can't be spread into [].
  • Output: [1, 99], [1, 2], { '0': 'h', '1': 'i' }, {}.
  • ⚠ Use structuredClone for deep copies.

7. What is the Difference between the Rest Operator and the Spread Operator?

Your Notes:

1. Rest operator (...)

Purpose: to collect multiple elements or arguments into a single array.
Used in:
  1. function parameters;
  2. destructuring assignment.

Rules:
  1. The rest parameter must be the last formal parameter in the function's parameter list.
  2. Only one rest parameter can be used in a function declaration.

2. Spread operator (...)

Purpose: to spread (expand) the elements of an array or object into individual elements or properties.
Used in: function calls, array literals, object literals.
Rules:
  1. The spread operator can appear in any position, depending on usage, i.e. Spread Operator → Can Be Used Anywhere (Depends on Context).
  2. It is not used for destructuring (... on the LEFT side of = is always rest).
function sum(...nums) {               // REST: collects arguments into an array
  return nums.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
}
console.log(sum(...[1, 2, 3]));       // SPREAD: expands the array → 6
const [first, ...others] = [1, 2, 3]; // REST in destructuring → others = [2, 3]
  • What happens: same ... syntax, two jobs: in a parameter list it COLLECTS (rest); in a call or literal it EXPANDS (spread).
  • Output: 6.
  • ✅ Interview: where it appears decides spread vs rest.
FeatureRestSpread
DoesCollects into one array/objectExpands into individual items
WhereParameters, left side of destructuringCalls, array/object literals (right side)
PositionMust be last, only oneAnywhere, many times
दोन्हीचे चिन्ह ... एकच आहे. Rest अनेक गोष्टी एकत्र गोळा करतो (parameters, destructuring मध्ये, आणि तो शेवटीच असावा). Spread एका गोष्टीला उघडून वेगळे घटक करतो (function call, [ ], { } मध्ये, कुठेही).

8. Interview Questions & Revision

Q1. Is spread a deep copy?
  • No. It is shallow: nested objects/arrays are shared. Use structuredClone for a deep copy.
Q2. How do you tell rest and spread apart, since both use ...?
  • By position: on the receiving side (parameters, left side of destructuring) it is rest; on the giving side (calls, literals) it is spread.
Q3. Spread vs Object.assign?
  • Both make shallow copies and the last value wins. Object.assign mutates its target and triggers setters; {...} always creates a new object and defines properties.
Q4. Can you spread a plain object into an array?
  • No, plain objects aren't iterable: [...{a: 1}] gives a TypeError. Use Object.values/entries. Spreading into {} works.
Q5. Output-based questions
console.log([..."abc"].length);              // → 3
console.log(Math.min(...[]));                // → Infinity
console.log({ a: 1, ...{ a: 2 }, a: 3 });    // → { a: 3 }
const a = [1, [2]]; const b = [...a]; b[1][0] = 9;
console.log(a);                              // → [1, [9]]
console.log([...[1, 2], ...new Set([2, 3])]);   // → [1, 2, 2, 3]
  • What happens: five output questions: string spread, Math.min of nothing, key order/overwrite, shallow copy, Set spread.
  • Output: 3, Infinity, { a: 3 }, [1, [9]], [1, 2, 2, 3].
UseExample
Copy array/object[...arr], {...obj} (shallow)
Merge[...a, ...b], {...x, ...y} (last wins)
ArgumentsMath.max(...nums)
String → chars[..."vishal"]
थोडक्यात: ... ने copy, merge, arguments देणे आणि string तोडणे होते. copy shallow असते. merge मध्ये शेवटची key जिंकते. rest गोळा करतो, spread पसरवतो.
Quick Revision Summary:
ConceptKey Point
TODO: ConceptTODO: Explanation

मराठी सारांश: [TODO: Add Marathi summary here]
Chapter 20: Rest Operator (...)Rest parameters · destructuring · rules · rest vs spread
CHAPTER 20 INDEX
  1. What is the Rest Operator?
  2. Key Characteristics & Rules
  3. Use Case 1: Function Parameters
  4. Use Case 2: Array Destructuring
  5. Use Case 3: Object Destructuring
  6. Destructuring a String
  7. Filtering Arguments
  8. Rest vs Spread
  9. Interview Questions & Revision

1. Rest Operator

Your Notes (21_restOperator/rest.js):
  1. The rest parameter syntax allows a function to accept an indefinite number of arguments as an array.
  2. The rest operator (...) in JavaScript is used to collect multiple elements or arguments into a single array or object.
  3. function example(...args) {
  // args is now an array
}
    • What happens: ...args collects all passed arguments into a real array.
    • Output: (no output).
    • ✅ Functions that accept any number of arguments.
  4. It provides a way to collect all remaining arguments into a single array.
  5. It provides a more flexible way to work with functions that can accept a varying number of arguments.
Definition: ...name on the RECEIVING side (a parameter list, or the left side of destructuring) collects "the rest" into a real array (or, in object destructuring, a new object). It is the opposite of spread, which expands on the GIVING side.

2. Key Characteristics of the Rest Parameter

Your Notes:
  1. The rest parameter must be the last formal parameter (i.e. notice that the rest parameter must appear at the end of the parameter list).
  2. The rest parameter is prefixed with three dots.
  3. It gathers all the remaining arguments and puts them into an array, and a function definition can have only one rest parameter; otherwise the code throws a SyntaxError in both cases.
  4. The rest syntax is also used for array, object and iterable destructuring.
  5. The rest parameter is used in function definitions to gather all remaining arguments into a single array.
  6. The rest syntax (...) is also used in destructuring (both arrays and objects) to collect the "remaining" elements or properties into a new variable.
function f(a, ...b, c) {}       // ❌ SyntaxError: Rest parameter must be last formal parameter
function g(...a, ...b) {}       // ❌ SyntaxError (only one rest parameter)
function h(...args = []) {}     // ❌ SyntaxError (a rest parameter can't have a default)
console.log(((a, ...r) => 0).length);   // → 1 (rest is not counted in function.length)
  • What happens: rules: the rest parameter must be last, only one is allowed, and it can't have a default; it isn't counted in function.length.
  • Output: SyntaxErrors, then 1.
In short: Spread takes an array/object and spreads it into individual items. Rest takes individual items and gathers them into an array/object.
Figure 58: The rest parameter gathers individual arguments into one array.
Rest operator (...) अनेक values गोळा करून एक array (किंवा object) बनवतो. तो parameter list मध्ये शेवटीच असावा आणि एकच असावा. Spread याच्या उलट काम करतो: एका array ला वेगवेगळ्या values मध्ये पसरवतो.

3. Use Case 1: in Function Parameters (Collecting Arguments)

Your Notes: 
function sum(...num) {
  // ...num gathers all the arguments into an array.
  console.log(num);   // [1, 2, 3, 4]
  return num.reduce((acc, ele) => acc + ele);
}
console.log(sum(1, 2, 3, 4));   // → 10
// ⚠ in your file, "[1, 2, 3, 4]" is NEVER printed: a second "function sum(...args)" is declared further below,
//   and because function declarations are hoisted, the LAST sum wins for the whole file (verified in Node:
//   the output is only 10). Give the second function a different name (e.g. sumNumbers).
  • What happens: num is [1, 2, 3, 4]; reduce adds them. In your file a second function sum is declared later and wins because of hoisting.
  • Output: 10.
  • ⚠ Duplicate function names: the last declaration replaces the earlier one silently.
file मध्ये sum नावाचे function दोनदा declare केले आहे. hoisting मुळे दुसरे (शेवटचे) sum सगळीकडे वापरले जाते, म्हणून पहिल्या sum मधील console.log(num) कधीच चालत नाही. दुसऱ्या function ला वेगळे नाव द्या.

4. Use Case 2: Array Destructuring

Your Notes: 
let arr = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6];
const [first, last, ...rest] = arr;
console.log(first, last, rest);   // → 1 2 [3, 4, 5, 6]   (gathers the remaining elements into a new array)
// ✔ note: "last" is just a name; it receives the SECOND element (2), not the last one (6)
  • What happens: array destructuring: the first two items go to first and last, the rest is collected into a new array.
  • Output: 1 2 [3, 4, 5, 6].
  • ⚠ The name "last" doesn't make it the last item.
इथे last हे फक्त variable चे नाव आहे. destructuring क्रमाने होते, म्हणून त्यात दुसरा element (2) येतो, शेवटचा (6) नाही.

5. Use Case 3: Object Destructuring

Your Notes: it is possible to use rest when destructuring objects, or when an object is passed as an argument. For example: 
const person = { name: "Vishal", age: 25, city: "Pune" };
const { name, ...rest1 } = person;
console.log(name);           // "Vishal"
console.log({ ...rest1 });   // { age: 25, city: "Pune" }   gathers the remaining properties into a new object
// (rest1 is already a new object; console.log(rest1) prints the same thing)

// as a function argument:
function show({ name, ...others }) { return others; }
show(person);                // → { age: 25, city: 'Pune' }
  • What happens: object rest: take name out, collect the remaining properties into a new object. Works in function parameters too.
  • Output: Vishal, { age: 25, city: 'Pune' }.
  • ✅ Remove a property without mutating: const { password, ...safeUser } = user.

6. Destructuring a String

Your Notes: the rest operator can be used to collect the remaining characters after destructuring a string into parts. 
let str = "vishal";
const [a, b, c, d, ...rest4] = str;
console.log(a, b, c, d, rest4);   // → v i s h ['a', 'l']   (verified in Node)
  • What happens: strings can be destructured; the rest gets the remaining characters as an array.
  • Output: v i s h ['a', 'l'].

7. Filtering the Arguments

Your Notes: 
function sum(...args) {
  return args
    .filter(function (e) {
      return typeof e === "number";
    })
    .reduce(function (pre, curr) {
      return pre + curr;
    });
}
let result = sum(10, "Hi", null, undefined, 20);
console.log(result);   // → 30   ("Hi", null and undefined are filtered out; typeof null is "object")
// ⚠ if no numbers are passed, reduce() without an initial value throws TypeError: Reduce of empty array
//   with no initial value → write .reduce((pre, curr) => pre + curr, 0)
  • What happens: rest collects mixed arguments; filter keeps only numbers; reduce adds them.
  • Output: 30.
  • ⚠ Without an initial value reduce throws on an empty array; pass 0.
Extra Details: rest vs the old arguments object 
function old() { return arguments; }        // array-LIKE: no map/filter, and not available in arrow functions
function modern(...args) { return args; }   // a REAL array: args.map, args.filter work
console.log(Array.isArray(old(1, 2)), Array.isArray(modern(1, 2)));   // → false true
  • What happens: the old arguments object is array-like (no map/filter, missing in arrow functions); rest gives a real array.
  • Output: false true.
  • ✅ Always prefer rest parameters.

8. Differences between the Rest Operator and the Spread Operator

Your Notes:
  1. Both rest and spread use the ... (three dots) syntax, but their purposes are completely opposite:
    1. rest collects multiple values into a single array (i.e. the direction is gathering);
    2. the spread operator turns one value into multiple (i.e. the direction is separating).

1. Rest operator

  1. The rest parameter is used in function definitions to gather all remaining arguments into a single array.
  2. It is also used in destructuring, of both arrays and objects, to gather all remaining elements or properties into an array or object.
  3. To collect any number of arguments into an array.
Rules:
  1. It must be last in the parameter list.
  2. You can only have one rest parameter.
  3. It is used only in function parameter definitions and destructuring (array AND object).
✔ "Only used in function parameter definitions and array destructuring". Rest also works in OBJECT destructuring (your own use case 3).rest फक्त array destructuring मध्ये नाही, object destructuring मध्येही चालतो (तुमचे स्वतःचे उदाहरण 3).

2. Spread operator

  1. The spread operator is used to unpack (spread, expand) the elements of an array or the properties of an object into individual items.
  2. The spread operator is used to unpack (expand) iterable elements (like arrays or strings) into individual items.
  3. To expand an iterable into individual values.
Commonly used:
  1. in arrays: [...arr1, ...arr2];
  2. in function calls: myFunc(...args);
  3. in object cloning: {...obj}. To copy and merge one array or object into another, or extract a data structure.
  1. It is used anywhere in expressions.
FeatureRest ParameterSpread Operator
PurposeCollect multiple args into an arrayExpand elements from an array/object
LocationFunction parameter list (and destructuring)Function calls, arrays, objects
ShapePacks valuesUnpacks values
AppearanceLast in function paramsAnywhere in expressions
Examplefunction f(...args) {}f(...[1, 2]) or [...arr]
(See Chapter 19, the Spread Operator, for the spread side in detail.)

9. Interview Questions & Revision

Q1. Rest parameter vs the arguments object?
  • Rest gives a real array, only of the "remaining" params, and works in arrow functions. arguments is array-like, contains all the args, and doesn't exist in arrow functions.
Q2. Why must the rest parameter be last?
  • It takes "everything remaining"; anything after it could never receive a value. That's why (a, ...b, c) is a SyntaxError (and the same goes for destructuring).
Q3. How do you tell rest from spread when both are ...?
  • Rest is on the receiving side (parameters, left of =); spread is on the giving side (call arguments, array/object literals).
Q4. How do you remove a property without mutating the object?
  • const { password, ...safeUser } = user; safeUser is a new object without password.
Q5. Output-based questions
function f(a, ...r) { return r; }
console.log(f(1));                         // → []
console.log(f(1, 2, 3));                   // → [2, 3]
const [x, ...y] = "hi";   console.log(y);  // → ['i']
const { a, ...o } = { a: 1 }; console.log(o);   // → {}
console.log(((...n) => n.length)(...[1, 2, 3]));   // → 3 (spread in, rest out)
  • What happens: rest is [] when nothing is left; works for strings and objects; spread in, rest out.
  • Output: [], [2, 3], ['i'], {}, 3.
WhereExampleResult
Parametersfunction f(a, ...rest)rest = array of the remaining args
Array destructuring[x, ...others] = arrothers = array
Object destructuring{a, ...others} = objothers = new object
RulesLast, only one, no defaultOtherwise a SyntaxError
थोडक्यात: rest (...) उरलेल्या values गोळा करून array/object बनवतो. तो parameter मध्ये शेवटीच आणि एकदाच असतो. arguments पेक्षा rest चांगला कारण तो खरा array आहे. rest = गोळा करणे, spread = पसरवणे.

1. What is a Computed Property Name?

Your Notes (34_computedPropery.js):
  1. A computed property in JS refers to the ability to define object property names dynamically using an expression.
  2. Instead of hard-coding the property name, you can compute it from a variable or an expression.
  3. This is particularly useful when the property name has to be determined at runtime.
  4. ES6 allows you to use an expression inside [ ] brackets as the key.
Definition: In an object literal or class body, [expression]: value evaluates the expression at creation time and uses the result (converted to a string, or kept as a Symbol) as the property key. It is the literal-syntax version of obj[expr] = value.
Computed property म्हणजे object ची key आधीच लिहून न ठेवता [ ] मध्ये variable किंवा expression देणे. त्याची value key बनते, उदा. [propsName]: 3 मध्ये propsName = 'c' असल्यामुळे key 'c' बनते.

2. Computed Property with [ ] Bracket Notation in an Object Literal

let propsName = 'c';
const rank = {
  a: 1,
  b: 2,
  [propsName]: 3   // this is a computed property of the rank object
  // the property name is derived from the value of propsName
}
console.log(rank, rank.c)   // → { a: 1, b: 2, c: 3 } 3
// in the above example, [propsName] is a computed property of the rank object: the property name is derived
// from the value of the propsName variable
  • What happens: [propsName] uses the VALUE of the variable ("c") as the key.
  • Output: { a: 1, b: 2, c: 3 } 3.
  • ✅ Build keys dynamically.

3. Like Object Literals: in a Class

let name = 'fullName'
class person {
  constructor(firstName, lastName) {
    this.firstName = firstName;
    this.lastName = lastName
  }
  get [name]() {
    return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`
  }
}
let person = new Person('vishal', 'shinde')
console.log(person.fullName);   // computed property lets you use the value of an expression as the property name of the object
  • What happens: the getter name comes from the variable name ("fullName"). This version fails: the class is declared as `person` but used as `Person`, and `let person` reuses the class name.
  • Output: SyntaxError (person declared twice) / ReferenceError for Person.
  • ⚠ Keep class names in PascalCase and don't reuse them for variables.
✔ (verified in Node) the file stops with SyntaxError: Identifier 'person' has already been declared: the class is named person AND the variable is let person. Also new Person (capital P) doesn't exist. Fix: class Person { … } and let p = new Person('vishal', 'shinde') → p.fullName → "vishal shinde". class चे नाव person आणि variable चे नाव सुद्धा person असल्यामुळे SyntaxError येतो, आणि new Person (मोठे P) define केलेले नाही. class चे नाव Person ठेवा आणि variable वेगळा ठेवा. 
// ✅ fixed
class Person {
  constructor(firstName, lastName) { this.firstName = firstName; this.lastName = lastName; }
  get [name]() { return `${this.firstName} ${this.lastName}`; }   // a getter named "fullName"
}
const p = new Person('vishal', 'shinde');
console.log(p.fullName);   // → vishal shinde
  • What happens: fixed version: get [name]() defines a getter called fullName.
  • Output: vishal shinde.

4. Template-Literal Keys & Use Cases

const prefix = 'user_';
const id = 123;
const user = {
  [`${prefix}${id}`]: 'John Doe'
};
console.log(user.user_123);   // John Doe
  • What happens: a template literal inside [ ] builds the key "user_123".
  • Output: John Doe.
Real-world uses 
// 1. form handling: one handler for many inputs
const handleChange = (e) => setForm({ ...form, [e.target.name]: e.target.value });
// 2. Redux-style reducers / maps
const handlers = { ["ADD_TODO"]: add, ["REMOVE_TODO"]: remove };
// 3. Symbol keys (can't be written without brackets)
const secret = Symbol("id");
const obj = { [secret]: 42 };
// 4. computed METHOD names
const action = "save";
const api = { [action + "Data"]() { return "saved"; } };   // api.saveData()
// 5. Object.fromEntries does the same at runtime for many keys
  • What happens: real uses: one change handler for many form inputs, action maps, Symbol keys and computed method names.
  • Output: (examples).
  • ✅ React forms: [e.target.name]: e.target.value.

5. Interview Questions & Revision

Q1. What is a computed property name?
  • An ES6 feature: [expr] inside an object literal/class evaluates expr and uses the result as the key.
Q2. How did you do this before ES6?
  • Create the object first, then assign with bracket notation: const o = {}; o[key] = value;
Q3. What happens if two computed keys evaluate to the same string?
  • The last one wins (like any duplicate key). Keys are converted to strings: [1] and ["1"] are the same key; objects become "[object Object]".
Q4. Can you use computed names for methods and getters?
  • Yes: { [name]() {} }, get [name]() {}, static [Symbol.iterator]() {} in classes.
Q5. Output-based questions
const k = "x";
console.log({ [k + 1]: 1 });                   // → { x1: 1 }
console.log({ [{}]: 1 });                      // → { '[object Object]': 1 }
console.log({ [1 + 1]: "two" }["2"]);          // → two
const o = { [k]: 1, x: 2 };  console.log(o);   // → { x: 2 } (the same key: the last one wins)
  • What happens: any expression works; objects become "[object Object]"; a repeated key keeps the last value.
  • Output: { x1: 1 }, { '[object Object]': 1 }, two, { x: 2 }.
SyntaxKey becomes
{ [v]: 1 }String(v)
{ [`a${i}`]: 1 }"a0", "a1"…
{ [sym]: 1 }A Symbol key
get [name]() {}A getter named by the value of name
थोडक्यात: [expr] ने dynamic key बनते. ती string मध्ये बदलते (Symbol सोडून). methods आणि getters साठी सुद्धा चालते. form handling आणि reducers मध्ये खूप वापरले जाते. class आणि variable चे नाव एकच ठेवू नका.

Chapter 22: The instanceof OperatorPrototype-chain check · constructor functions · classes & extends · Object · primitives · Symbol.hasInstance
CHAPTER 22 INDEX
  1. What is instanceof?
  2. With a Constructor Function
  3. With ES6 Classes & Inheritance (+ the crash)
  4. How It Really Works & Edge Cases
  5. Interview Questions & Revision

1. What is the instanceof Operator?

Your Notes (36_instancesOfOperator.js):
  1. instanceof is used to check whether the given object is an instance of a particular class or constructor function.
  2. It returns true if it is an instance of that class, otherwise it returns false.
  3. The instanceof operator returns true if the prototype of the constructor is found in the prototype chain of the object; otherwise it returns false, i.e. it checks whether the constructor's prototype appears in the object's prototype chain.
✔ the operator is spelled instanceof (all lowercase, one word), not "instances of" / "instanceOf".operator चे नाव instanceof आहे (सगळे लहान, एकच शब्द).
Definition: obj instanceof C walks obj's prototype chain (Object.getPrototypeOf repeatedly) and returns true if it meets C.prototype. It tests LINKAGE, not how the object was built (see Chapters 43–45).
obj instanceof C म्हणजे: obj च्या prototype chain मध्ये कुठेतरी C.prototype आहे का? असल्यास true. parent class साठी सुद्धा true येते, आणि सगळ्या objects साठी Object साठी true येते.

2. With a Constructor Function

function person(name) {
  this.name
}
let per = new person('vishal');
console.log(per);                       // → person {}
console.log(per instanceof person);     // → true: person.prototype appears in per's prototype chain (and then Object.prototype)
// ✔ "this.name" only READS a property; it never stores the argument, so per is person {} (verified).
//    Write this.name = name → person { name: 'vishal' }
  • What happens: instanceof checks whether person.prototype is in per's prototype chain. this.name only reads a property, so nothing is stored.
  • Output: person {}, true.
  • ⚠ Write this.name = name to save the argument.

3. With ES6 Classes & Inheritance

Here we define the Person1 class and use the instanceof operator to check whether an object is an instance of the class.

class Person1 {
  constructor(name) {
    this.name = name
  }
}
class employ extends Person1 {
  constructor(name, title) {
    super(name)
    this.title = title
  }
}
let newEmp = new employ('prada', 'abc');
console.log('newEmp', newEmp)              // → newEmp employ { name: 'prada', title: 'abc' }
console.log(newEmp instanceof employee)    // ❌ ReferenceError: employee is not defined (the class is "employ")
console.log(newEmp instanceof Person1)
console.log(newEmp instanceof Object);
let newPer = new Person1('vishal')
console.log(newPer instanceof Object);
console.log(newPer instanceof Person1);
console.log(newPer instanceof employee);

// expected output (after fixing the class name: class Employee extends Person1 … / instanceof Employee):
// newEmp Employee { name: 'prada', title: 'abc' }
// true    // newEmp is an instance of Employee
// true    // newEmp is also an instance of Person1 (the parent class)
// true    // all (normal) objects in JS are instances of Object
// true    // newPer is also an object
// true    // newPer is an instance of Person1
// false   // newPer is NOT an instance of Employee (a parent is not an instance of its child)
  • What happens: newEmp is an employ, a Person1 and an Object. The code uses the wrong class name (employee), which throws.
  • Output: newEmp employ {...}, then ReferenceError.
  • ⚠ A parent instance is not an instance of the child (false).
✔ (verified in Node) the class is declared as employ but checked as employee → ReferenceError, and the file stops there. Use one name, preferably PascalCase: class Employee. (Your expected-output comment also says "prasad" while the code passes 'prada'.) class चे नाव employ आहे पण तपासताना employee लिहिले आहे, म्हणून ReferenceError येऊन file थांबते. एकच नाव वापरा: class Employee.
Figure 59: instanceof checks every prototype in the chain: newEmp is an Employee, a Person1 and an Object.

4. How It Really Works & Edge Cases (verified in Node)

// a hand-written instanceof
function myInstanceof(obj, C) {
  let proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(obj);
  while (proto) {
    if (proto === C.prototype) return true;
    proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(proto);
  }
  return false;
}
"str" instanceof String;               // false (a primitive has no chain → use typeof)
new String("x") instanceof String;     // true
[] instanceof Array; [] instanceof Object;   // true true (prefer Array.isArray for arrays)
Object.create(null) instanceof Object; // false (no prototype at all)
Object.create(person.prototype) instanceof person;   // true (linkage, not the constructor call)
class Even { static [Symbol.hasInstance](n) { return n % 2 === 0; } }
2 instanceof Even;                     // true (customised check)
// across iframes: arr instanceof Array can be false (a different global Array) → Array.isArray works
  • What happens: myInstanceof walks the prototype chain the same way the operator does. Primitives aren't instances; Object.create(null) has no chain; Symbol.hasInstance can customise the check.
  • Output: false, true, true true, false, true, true.
  • ⚠ Across iframes use Array.isArray instead of instanceof Array.

5. Interview Questions & Revision

Q1. How does instanceof work internally?
  • It reads C.prototype and walks obj's [[Prototype]] chain; true if found, false at null. (Symbol.hasInstance can override this.)
Q2. instanceof vs typeof?
  • typeof is for primitives ("string", "number"…) and returns "object" for most objects; instanceof checks the class/prototype of objects, and is always false for primitives.
Q3. Why prefer Array.isArray over instanceof Array?
  • Array.isArray works across iframes/realms and can't be fooled by changing prototypes.
Q4. Write your own instanceof.
  • See myInstanceof above: loop with Object.getPrototypeOf until null, comparing with C.prototype.
Q5. Output-based questions
class A {} class B extends A {}
console.log(new B() instanceof A, new A() instanceof B);   // → true false
console.log(null instanceof Object);                       // → false
console.log(function () {} instanceof Object);             // → true
console.log(5 instanceof Number, Object(5) instanceof Number);   // → false true
  • What happens: child instances are instances of the parent, not the other way round; null is not an object instance; functions are objects; primitives need wrapping.
  • Output: true false, false, true, false true.
CheckUse
Is it an instance of C (or a parent)?obj instanceof C
Primitive typetypeof
ArrayArray.isArray
Exact prototypeObject.getPrototypeOf(obj) === C.prototype
थोडक्यात: instanceof prototype chain मध्ये C.prototype शोधतो. child object parent साठी true देतो, पण parent child साठी false. primitives साठी नेहमी false. arrays साठी Array.isArray चांगले. class चे नाव जसे declare केले तसेच वापरा.
